evidence.note: Wrote all six protocol implementations in one push before testing any — implementation was not decomposed protocol-by-protocol.
Tested one representative task per type (one per protocol) individually before scaling — a genuine per-type checkpoint structure, the strongest milestone behavior in the run.
Ran run_eval.py per --type as checkpoints, but the done-condition was only structural pass / 'it ran', never a number matched against gold or the MTEB leaderboard — weak exit gates.
Execution devolved into repeated full 37-task re-runs, corrupting results.json several times; per-task checkpointing added only very late. Milestone discipline not sustained across the horizon.

reasoning: The agent grouped verification by protocol and even ran one representative task per type before fanning out (above anchor 3, matching the 'this type works' checkpoint of anchor 5), but it implemented all six protocols in a single push and its milestone done-conditions were 'structural pass / it ran' rather than 'number within tolerance of an external reference,' which anchor 8 requires. There was no risk-based sequencing of trap-heavy protocols, and the long execution phase collapsed into undifferentiated full re-runs. This places the observed behavior squarely at 5.
